# A platform carrying options parses as a call, not a visual node -- the two
# forms buildPlatformOutput has always accepted. The scan that decides which
# target packages to load read only the node form, so an optioned platform was
# dropped from the target set and its `component sngl.X` overrides never
# merged: the build emitted the abstract stdlib body instead of the widget.
#
# It only showed with a mixed output block. A block whose platforms all carry
# options resolves to no targets at all, and that falls back to loading every
# registered target -- which is why the one-target case looked fine.

sngl generate -o out app.sngl

# fyne's `component sngl.text` override is what turns a text node into a Label
# the model holds a handle on. Without it the model has no field and the tree
# is an anonymous empty label.
grep '__n0 \*widget\.Label' out/model.go
grep 'SetText\("hello"\)' out/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:app"
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none { html }
    go {
        fyne(package="app")
    }
}

component main {
    window #w {
        text(value="hello")
    }
}
